answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed if peers prove fraud. A new identity starts at zero trust, so an attacker must fund every fake separately, and the cost ripples outward as each clone needs its own deposit, work history, and endorsements. Like climbers reaching a summit, agents earn higher limits only after sustained honest tasks, while a zephyr of cheap throwaway accounts cannot pass because each one still pays the full stake and waiting period.
